history.dynasty: Kalachuri of Ratnapura — King Ratnadeva I (original); current structure Vikram Samvat 1552 (1492 CE) by King Bahar Sai
history.period: 12th-13th century (original shrine); present structure 1492 CE; renovated by the Archaeological Survey of India
history.summary: The Mahamaya Temple at Ratanpur is one of the 52 Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Goddess Mahamaya — worshipped as Durga/Mahalakshmi and as Kosaleswari, presiding deity of the old Dakshin Kosal region (modern Chhattisgarh). Built during the reign of the Kalachuris of Ratnapura at the spot where King Ratnadeva is said to have had a darshan of Goddess Kali, the shrine originally housed three goddesses — Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati; later a new temple was built by King Bahar Sai in Vikram Samvat 1552 (1492 CE) for Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati, with the twin idols seen today (Mahishasuramardini in front, Saraswati behind). It is traditionally the Kuldevi of the Ratanpur state, and pilgrims also visit the Kalabhairava temple on the approach road to complete the pilgrimage. CONFLICTS: sources differ on which part of Sati fell here — 'wing' (velpu) versus 'right skanda' (Drishti IAS). CSV CORRECTIONS: name 'Mahalaxmi Temple' is approximate — the documented temple is the Mahamaya (Mahalakshmi) Temple; town 'Bilaspur' is the district headquarters ~25 km away — corrected to Ratanpur. name: Mahamaya Temple
town_description: Ratanpur, about 25 km from Bilaspur, was the capital of the Kalachuri kings of Ratnapura and is known as the city of temples and ponds. Its Mahamaya temple is one of the 52 Shakti Peethas, and Khutaghat Dam is its nearby picnic and pilgrimage spot.

travel.airport: Bilaspur airport is the nearest; Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur (approx. 125 km) is the major airport.
travel.road: Ratanpur is about 25 km from Bilaspur by road; the Kalabhairava temple stands on the approach road and is visited to complete the pilgrimage.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Navaratri (Jyoti Kalash) is the most vibrant time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily; exact darshan hours are not published online — verify locally before travel.
